title: Tanzanian Mango Sorbet
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Mango Sorbet — Zanzibar Dodo mango purée frozen with lime juice and a light cardamom syrup. Pure mango, pure Zanzibar — the most refreshing dessert the island produces. No dairy, no fat, just the extraordinary flavour of peak-season mango.
longDesc: Mango sorbet from Zanzibar's own Dodo mango is one of the finest frozen desserts in the world — the mango's extraordinary fragrance and natural sweetness need minimal intervention. Just lime for brightness, cardamom for the Zanzibar signature, and a simple syrup to produce the right texture.
ingredients: 4 large ripe Zanzibar mangoes — peeled and diced (about 600g flesh)
steps: Make syrup: dissolve sugar in water with cardamom. Simmer 2 minutes. Cool completely.
Blend mango flesh until completely smooth.
Combine mango purée, cooled syrup, lime juice, and salt.
Pour into a shallow freezer container.
Freeze 4 hours, whisking vigorously every hour (or churn in an ice cream machine for 20 minutes).
Serve in chilled glasses or scooped into bowls.
chefTips: The ripest, most fragrant mango produces the finest sorbet.
Whisking every hour during freezing breaks up ice crystals — producing a smoother result without a machine.
Serve at -12°C — slightly softer than ice cream.
commonMistakes: Not whisking during freezing — large ice crystals.
cookingScience: Sorbet texture depends on small ice crystal size. The sugar syrup lowers the freezing point — allowing the sorbet to be scoopable at -12 to -15°C rather than rock-hard. Whisking during freezing mechanically breaks up forming ice crystals, maintaining a smooth texture. The natural acids in mango and lime also slightly inhibit large crystal formation.
sustainabilityTips: Zanzibar mango in peak season — maximum nutrition, zero food miles.
storage: Freeze up to 3 weeks. Soften 5 minutes before scooping.
healthBenefits: Very high vitamin C and beta-carotene.
culturalNote: Zanzibar mango sorbet is the island's most honest frozen dessert — the Dodo mango is extraordinary enough to need nothing but a clean technique. To eat it in Zanzibar during mango season is to taste the island at its peak.
